items.title: Sunday hearing passes with no release order for Das and Ranka; SEM discusses threats, NCR registered
items.summary: Five-day judicial custody of Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka ended Sunday (Oct 18), but a hearing before Special Executive Magistrate ACP Mahesh Kumar Meena — which started ~5:30 PM, five hours late per PTI — ended with NO order passed on their release. The 10-15 minute hearing dwelt on alleged threats received by the SEM over the leaders' release; the public prosecutor said the matter needed investigation. Delhi Police later confirmed a non-cognisable report (NCR) was registered against unidentified persons over the SEM's complaint. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke accused authorities of 'dirty tricks' to delay proceedings; legal head Ratna Singh (PTI) said four sureties were rejected on 'vague' grounds and questioned why a threatening message should stall the release case. CJP says it will pursue legal remedies before higher judicial forums.

items.title: Das and Ranka's judicial custody extended by two more days; sureties rejected, Tihar till Oct 21
items.summary: A newly-appointed Special Executive Magistrate (Ritu Raj) at Mandir Marg police station on Monday evening extended Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka's judicial custody by two days, till October 21, at Delhi Police's request. The order cited their likelihood of re-offending (alleged breach of peace bonds), police claims they 'can't be trusted,' and law-and-order concerns during the festive Dussehra period; it found their behaviour showed 'no respect for law.' Sureties furnished for release were rejected — including a photo mismatch between a surety's bail-bond photograph and Aadhaar card — and fresh sureties were demanded. CJP legal head Ratna Singh called it 'an absolute mockery of the judicial system' and said the order will be challenged in a higher court. Dipke shared smiling photos of the two after five days in Tihar, writing their spirits were unbroken.

items.event_time_ist: Oct 19 (first case Monday; second case Oct 20)
items.title: Delhi Police transfers both Das-Ranka cases to Crime Branch's Inter-State Cell
items.summary: Delhi Police transferred the criminal cases against Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka — the Oct 13 Jantar Mantar trespassing/protest case (FIRs at Connaught Place PS under BNS 223A/332/61(2) and Parliament Street PS) — to the Inter-State Cell of its Crime Branch on October 19, per police sources via PTI and LawBeat. A second case was transferred on Tuesday (Oct 20), making two cases now with the unit. The transfer came the same day the SEM extended their judicial custody by two days. CJP has framed the move as politicising routine protest policing; police say it reflects the seriousness of the matter.

items.title: Das and Ranka withdraw Delhi HC plea against custody extension; told to await 2 PM SEM hearing
items.summary: Cockroach Janta Party co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on Wednesday withdrew from the Delhi High Court their petition challenging the SEM's October 19 order extending their judicial custody till October 21. Justice Subramonium Prasad permitted the withdrawal and asked them to await the outcome of the SEM hearing scheduled later today (2 PM) to reconsider the sureties furnished, and to approach the appellate court if their grievance persists. The court clarified it had made no observations on the merits and orally observed that an Article 226 writ petition was not the appropriate remedy. Counsels had argued the Oct 19 extension order was legally unsustainable and that the SEM lacked jurisdiction. Earlier in the day, IANS reported the HC had agreed to an urgent hearing during the Dussehra vacation; counsel Ratna Singh said the duo should not spend 'a single minute behind bars' more than necessary.
items.source_name: The Hindu BusinessLine / ANI (via DevDiscourse) / IANS

items.title: Dipke pauses all CJP protests until Diwali; supporters told to spend festivals with families
items.summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke announced on Tuesday (Oct 20) in a ~16-minute video message that the party will hold no demonstrations or protest gatherings until Diwali, urging supporters — whom he calls 'cockroaches' — to spend the festive period with their families, noting the anxiety recent detentions have caused families (including his own and those of Das and Ranka). He praised the jailed leaders' courage ('smiles on the fifth day') and named Das and Ranka as the movement's primary decision-makers. In the same round of statements he rejected comparisons of the protests to youth unrest/regime changes in Nepal, Bangladesh and France, insisting the movement follows Gandhian Satyagraha and non-violence.
items.source_name: Hindustan Times (via InShorts) / Saptashwa TV / The CSR Journal

items.title: 30-ft cockroach effigy burnt with Ravana at Pitampura Dussehra; Dipke thanks organisers for 'free publicity'
items.summary: A 30-foot cockroach effigy was burnt alongside the traditional effigies of Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Meghnad at the Shri Keshav Ramlila Committee's Dussehra event at Netaji Subhash Place, Pitampura, on Tuesday evening. Committee president and BJP MLA Ashok Goel said the effigy symbolised filth and unhygienic conditions under the Swachh Bharat/Swachh Delhi campaigns and denied any political motive (he has previously burnt effigies of Naxalism and terrorism, per ANI). CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke sarcastically thanked the organisers on X: 'Thank you for the free publicity,' also sharing a scene from the film Swades. CJP legal head Ratna Singh dismissed the move as 'tamasha' (drama). AAP Delhi chief Saurabh Bharadwaj lodged a complaint with the Governor and the Delhi Police Commissioner against the organisers and sought an FIR; Delhi minister and BJP leader Kapil Mishra defended the burning, calling the cockroach a symbol of filth and disorder.
